items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I met the English trumpeter Humphrey Lyttelton for the first time.

ctx.x: We finished the 5th of February at the club and did the first concert of the tour at Le mans, where the famour 24 hours endurance auto races are held every year. We did 21 concerts and had three days off during the month. It was a difficult tour because that February broke all records in France for being the coldest of any year known in this country. The bad weather started about 3 days after we did the first concert. In some places we played it was so cold that not more than 25 people were brave enough to face…

We came back in Paris the second of March and flew to Algiers to play a big ball at the Hotel St. George and gave a concert at the Salle Borde the 3rd. The 10th of March I played what was called a New Orleans Festival at the Palais des Sports in Paris which featured bands from several European countries and I met the English trumpeter Humphrey Lyttelton for the first time. I had heard of him as he became England's best known jazz trumpet man after Nat Gonella who was the English Louis Armstrong in the 1930's.…

I had an engagement at the Alhambra theatre as a feature trumpetist and singer with Maxim Saury, the ex-Claude Bollong clarinetist who was making a name for himself as leader of a Dixieland group. Maxim had a trumpet player named Jean Claude Naude who recorded some numbers with Maxime and it was difficult at times to believe that it was not Satchmo himself. Naude came closer to getting the same tone as Pops than any trumpet player, I can think of, that copies Pops. And he had the phrasing down pat also.
